topics.label: Lecture Introduction and Learning Objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the lecturer, outlines the scope of the cancer lecture series, and defines the key learning objectives for the session.

topics.label: Intrinsic and Environmental Contributions to Cancer Etiology
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the fundamental causes of cancer by comparing intrinsic biological errors and genetic predispositions with environmental influences supported by global epidemiological data.

topics.label: Infectious Pathogens and Burkitt Lymphoma Pathogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics illustrate how infectious agents contribute to oncogenesis, using Burkitt lymphoma as a detailed case study of multi-factorial pathogen-driven cancer.

topics.label: Chemical and Physical Mutagens and Metabolic DNA Damage
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the biochemical mechanisms through which specific environmental chemicals, dietary toxins, and radiation undergo activation to induce DNA adducts and mutations.

topics.label: Tumor Promotion, Chronic Inflammation, and Host Susceptibility
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore non-mutagenic mechanisms of carcinogenesis, focusing on how tumor promoters, inflammatory microenvironments, and developmental tissue vulnerability drive clonal outgrowth.

topics.label: Experimental and Epidemiological Methods for Testing Carcinogenicity
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics outline the genomic, epidemiological, animal, and in vitro screening methodologies utilized to identify mutational signatures and evaluate whether substances are carcinogenic.

topics.label: Carcinogen Exposure Risk-Benefit Analysis and Lecture Summary
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic concludes the lecture by discussing practical risk-versus-benefit decisions regarding exposure to carcinogens and summarizing the main themes.
